q: The Mackey-Zimmer theorem classifies extensions of ergodic systems. An ergodic extension T̃ of an ergodic T (both systems on standard probability spaces) is a:
opts: Compact group extension: X̃ = X × G/H for a compact group G and closed subgroup H, with T̃(x,gH) = (Tx, α(x)·gH)
Skew product over a Kronecker system
exp: Mackey-Zimmer structure theorem: any ergodic extension is (up to isomorphism) a compact group extension (also called a homogeneous extension or induced extension). The cocycle α: X → G encodes the fibering. This is the key tool in the structure theory of ergodic systems (Host-Kra theory uses it for characteristic factors).
